title: Why Valpolicella tastes the way it does

lede.text: Valpolicella is a blend with Corvina and/or Corvinone at its core, from 45% to 95%. Rondinella, from 5% to 30%, completes it.

chapters.title: From the Adige bend at Ceraino
paras: The zone covers all or part of 19 municipalities, Verona among them. Its boundary line starts in the north, opposite Monte Rocca, on the cliff above a bend of the Adige near Ceraino.
From there the line runs through woodland at 410 m. Further on it passes north of Monte Pugna, at 740 m.

fly.label: The Adige bend at Ceraino
fly.caption: The zone's boundary starts on the cliff above a bend of the Adige near Ceraino.

chapters.title: A blend led by Corvina or Corvinone
paras: The grapes come from estate vineyards that hold Corvina Veronese (also called Cruina or Corvina) and/or Corvinone for 45% to 95%. Rondinella makes up 5% to 30%.

Up to 25% in total may come from other grapes. Red non-aromatic varieties approved for the province of Verona may make up to 15%, with no more than 10% of any one variety. The remaining 10% may come from red Italian native varieties approved for Verona.
The label may add "classico" or "Valpantena" as a reference, and "superiore" as a specification.
